''[[The Office (American TV series)|The Office]]'' is an American television [[sitcom]] broadcast on [[NBC]]. Created as an [[film adaptation|adaptation]] by [[Greg Daniels]] of the [[The Office (British TV series)|British series of the same name]], it is a [[mockumentary]] that follows the day-to-day lives of the employees of the [[Scranton, Pennsylvania]] branch of [[Dunder Mifflin]], a fictional paper supply company.<ref name="s1premiere">{{cite news |title=BBC to screen US TV's ''The Office'' |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/4315621.stm |work=[[BBC News]] |date=March 3, 2005 |access-date=June 19, 2008}}</ref> The series ran on NBC in the United States from March 24, 2005, to May 16, 2013. Additionally, nine spin-off series of [[webisode]]s  of ''The Office'' have been aired on NBC.com.

''The Office'' aired a short [[The Office (American season 1)|first season]] in 2005 that consisted of six episodes. This was followed by a full-length [[The Office (American season 2)|second season]] in 2005–06 that consisted of 22 episodes, and a [[The Office (American season 3)|third season]] in 2006–07, with 25 episodes. Due to the [[2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike]], the [[The Office (American season 4)|fourth season]] that aired in 2007–08 consisted of 19 episodes.<ref name="strike"/>  The [[The Office (American season 5)|fifth season]] aired during 2008–09 and consisted of 28 episodes. The [[The Office (American season 6)|sixth season]] aired during 2009–10 and consisted of 26 episodes. The [[The Office (American season 7)|seventh season]] aired during 2010–11 and consisted of 26 episodes. The [[The Office (American season 8)|eighth season]] aired during 2011–12 and consisted of 24 episodes. The [[The Office (American season 9)|ninth season]] aired during 2012–13 and consisted of 25 episodes. A total of 201 episodes of ''The Office'' aired over nine seasons.

The first set of webisodes, titled ''[[The Office: The Accountants|The Accountants]]'', consisted of ten episodes and ran between the second and third seasons. ''[[#Kevin's Loan (2008)|Kevin's Loan]]'' consisted of four episodes and ran between the fourth and fifth seasons. ''[[#The Outburst (2008)|The Outburst]]'' aired in the middle of the fifth season and consisted of four episodes. ''[[#Blackmail (2009)|Blackmail]]'' aired during the end of the fifth season and consisted of four episodes. ''[[#Subtle Sexuality (2009)|Subtle Sexuality]]'' aired during the beginning of the sixth season and consisted of three episodes. ''[[#The Mentor (2010)|The Mentor]]'' aired near the end of the sixth season and consisted of four episodes. ''[[#The 3rd Floor (2010)|The 3rd Floor]]'' aired during the beginning of the seventh season and consisted of three episodes. ''[[#The Podcast (2011)|The Podcast]]'' aired near the middle of the seventh season (was previously available on the season 6 DVD) and consisted of three episodes. The latest webisode series, ''[[#The Girl Next Door (2011)|The Girl Next Door]]'' aired at the end of the seventh season and had two episodes.

All nine seasons are available on DVD in [[DVD region code#Region codes and countries|regions]] 1, 2, and 4. Starting with season five, the series is available on [[Blu-ray]]. This list is ordered by the episodes' original air dates and not by the [[production code number]]s provided by NBC's official episode guide, which show the order in which episodes were filmed.<ref name="Episode Guide">{{cite web|url=http://www.nbc.com/The_Office/recaps/ |title=''The Office'' Episodes |publisher=NBC |access-date=November 20, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605044321/http://www.nbc.com/The_Office/recaps/ |archive-date=June 5, 2011 }}</ref>

After the acquisition of the series by the streaming service [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]], extended format episodes designated "Superfan Episodes" were released beginning in 2021 exclusive to Peacock, including deleted scenes and additional footage.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/723762/the-office-season-4-now-has-extended-superfan-episodes-on-peacock/ |title=The Office Season 4 Now Has Extended Superfan Episodes On Peacock |website=/Film |first=Jenna |last=Busch |date=January 4, 2022 |access-date=February 27, 2022}}</ref>

==Episodes==
===Season 1 (2005)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 1}}
Season one aired between March 24 and April 26, 2005. It originally debuted as a [[midseason replacement]] for [[Committed (American TV series)|''Committed'']].<ref>
[http://tv.zap2it.com/tveditorial/tve_main/1,1002,271|93084|1|,00.html "''Office,'' 'Jury' Report for NBC Duty in March"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070808093923/http://tv.zap2it.com/tveditorial/tve_main/1%2C1002%2C271%7C93084%7C1%7C%2C00.html |date=August 8, 2007 }} . Zap2It (January 21, 2005). Retrieved on April 3, 2008.
</ref> It carried over general plot ideas from the earlier British series created by [[Stephen Merchant]] and [[Ricky Gervais]], and particularly the threat of wholesale downsizing. However, only the pilot was a direct adaptation of one of the UK version's episodes.<ref name=s1>{{cite web | url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/10005079-office/ | website=Rotten Tomatoes | title=''The Office'': Season 01 (2005) | access-date=August 26, 2008 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080930181356/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/10005079-office/ | archive-date=September 30, 2008 | df=mdy-all }}</ref>

This season introduced the main characters, and established the general plot as a documentary crew is recording the lives of the employees of the fictitious [[Dunder Mifflin]] Paper Company. In a [[mockumentary]] format, it shows [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]] ([[Steve Carell]]), regional manager of the Scranton branch office, as he tries to convince the filmmakers of the documentary that he presides over a happy, well-running office. Meanwhile, sales rep [[Jim Halpert]] ([[John Krasinski]]) finds methods to undermine his cube-mate, [[Dwight Schrute]] ([[Rainn Wilson]]); receptionist [[Pam Beesly]] ([[Jenna Fischer]]) is trying to deal with Michael's insensitivities and flubs; and the temporary employee [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan Howard]] ([[B. J. Novak]]) is acting mostly as an observer of the insanity around him.<ref name=s1/>
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 1}}

===Season 2 (2005–06)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 2}}
Season two of ''The Office'' premiered on September 20, 2005, and ended on May 11, 2006.<ref name="s2premiere">{{cite magazine |first=Rick |last=Kissell |title=''Earl'' sterling in debut |url=https://variety.com/2005/scene/markets-festivals/earl-sterling-in-debut-1117929456/ |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=September 25, 2005 |access-date=June 19, 2008}}</ref><ref name="s2finale">{{cite web |url=http://tv.ign.com/objects/818/818735.html |title=''The Office'': Season 2  |access-date=June 19, 2008 |website=[[IGN]]}}</ref> NBC initially ordered only six episodes for the season, then in September ordered seven more.<ref>
[http://tv.zap2it.com/tveditorial/tve_main/1,1002,271|97778|1|,00.html "NBC Gives Bonus to ''The Office''"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071119103510/http://tv.zap2it.com/tveditorial/tve_main/1%2C1002%2C271%7C97778%7C1%7C%2C00.html |date=November 19, 2007 }} . Zap2It (September 29, 2005). Retrieved on April 22, 2008.
</ref> On November 3, 2005, NBC ordered an additional three,<ref>
[http://tv.zap2it.com/tveditorial/tve_main/1,1002,271|98411|1|,00.html  "NBC May Make More ''Office'' Space"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071111052954/http://tv.zap2it.com/tveditorial/tve_main/1%2C1002%2C271%7C98411%7C1%7C%2C00.html |date=November 11, 2007 }} . Zap2It (November 4, 2005). Retrieved on April 22, 2008.
</ref> and in the end it had ordered a full season of 22 episodes.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/office_season_2/| title=''The Office'' - Season 2 (2006) | website= Rotten Tomatoes| access-date=August 23, 2008}}</ref>

The second season storyline further delved into the fear of company downsizing, along with the introduction of new characters and developing some of the minor ones—especially that of Dwight.<ref>{{cite news| title=Laughter in the Workplace—The second season of ''The Office'' is as entertaining as the first|author=Stevens, Dana|date=December 19, 2003|access-date=August 23, 2008| url=http://www.slate.com/id/2092971| newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> As Michael begins a relationship with his boss [[Jan Levinson]] ([[Melora Hardin]]), Pam and Jim's relationship becomes one of the focal points of the season. Their compatibility becomes more obvious as Jim's feelings for Pam continue to grow, while she struggles with her engagement to warehouse worker [[Roy Anderson (The Office)|Roy Anderson]] ([[David Denman]]).
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 2}}

===Season 3 (2006–07)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 3}}
Season three premiered on September 21, 2006, and ended on May 17, 2007.<ref name="s3premiere">{{cite web|first=Neil |last=Wilkes |title=NBC announces Fall premiere dates |url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/tv/news/a35158/nbc-announces-fall-premiere-dates.html |website=[[Digital Spy]] |date=July 23, 2006 |access-date=June 19, 2008 }}</ref><ref name="s3finale">{{cite web |url=http://tv.ign.com/objects/838/838051.html |title=''The Office'': Season 3  |access-date=June 19, 2008 |website=[[IGN]]}}</ref> It featured 25 episodes, including two hour-long episodes, six "super-sized" episodes, and guest directors such as [[J. J. Abrams]], [[Joss Whedon]] and [[Harold Ramis]].<ref name="s3finale"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://tv.ign.com/articles/754/754846p1.html|title=Joss Whedon and J.J. Abrams Both Directing ''The Office''|website=IGN|date=January 11, 2007|access-date=September 11, 2008|last=Goldman|first=Eric}}</ref>

The season marked the move of main character [[Jim Halpert]] from Scranton to Stamford, and also introduced [[Rashida Jones]] as [[Karen Filippelli]], and [[Ed Helms]] as [[Andy Bernard]] (both members of Dunder Mifflin Stamford) as recurring characters.  Helms would later be promoted to series regular.  The main plot for the early episodes of the season deals with a recurring problem in seasons one and two—the problem of company downsizing—while in the latter half of the season, inter-office relationships also became a major plot point.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://dvd.ign.com/articles/816/816383p1.html | access-date=August 24, 2008 | website=IGN | title=''The Office'': Season 3 DVD Review | author1=Fickett, Travis | author2=Monfette, Christopher | date=August 28, 2007 | archive-date=June 27, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120627084913/http://dvd.ign.com/articles/816/816383p1.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>  [[Metacritic]], which assigns normalized ratings out of 100 to critics' reviews, calculated an average score of 85/100 based on five collected reviews, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-office/season-3 | title=''The Office'' Season Three | access-date=September 6, 2008 |website=Metacritic}}</ref>
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 3}}

===Season 4 (2007–08)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 4}}
NBC ordered a full fourth season of ''The Office'' consisting of 30 episodes, which included five one-hour specials.  However, the [[2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike]] shut down production for nearly five months in the middle of the season (between the episodes "[[The Deposition (The Office)|The Deposition]]" and "[[Dinner Party (The Office)|Dinner Party]]").<ref name="strike">{{cite press release |title=NBC Announces Broadcast Return of Several Scripted Series with Original Episodes in April |publisher=NBC Universal |date=February 13, 2008 |url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2008/02/13/nbc-announces-broadcast-return-of-several-scripted-series-with-original-episodes-in-april-26680/20080213nbc02/ |access-date=June 20, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release | date=January 17, 2007 | url = http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2007/01/17/nbc-renews-hit-series-the-office-my-name-is-earl-heroes-and-law-and-order-special-victims-unit-for-full-season-of-episodes-in-2007-08-23378/20070117nbc02/ |title = NBC renews hit series ''The Office'', ''My Name is Earl'', ''Heroes'', and ''Law & Order: Special Victims Unit'' for full season of episodes in 2007-08 | publisher= NBC Universal| access-date =April 12, 2008}}</ref> Because of the shutdown, the fourth season of ''The Office'' only consisted of 19 half-hour episodes, ten of which were paired as five separate hour-long episodes. The season premiered on September 27, 2007.

Season four marked the departure of Karen Filippelli as a regular character, although she appeared for a few seconds in the first episode, "[[Fun Run]]"; and was featured as the regional manager of the Utica branch in the tenth episode, "[[Branch Wars]]". Relationships emerged as the main theme of the season, with Jim and Pam's rising, as well as Michael and Jan's and Dwight and Angela's declining.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://tv.ign.com/articles/875/875898p1.html| website=IGN | access-date=August 23, 2008|  title=''The Office'': Season 4 Review|author=Fickett, Travis|date=May 22, 2008}}</ref>  Technology was another theme as the office staff struggled with initiatives introduced by Ryan to modernize the company.<ref>{{cite magazine| url=https://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20149876,00.html| magazine=Entertainment Weekly| title=PDA Problems| access-date=August 24, 2008| author=Fenno, Christine| date=October 7, 2007| archive-date=January 31, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130131032741/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20149876,00.html| url-status=dead}}</ref>
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 4}}

===Season 5 (2008–09)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 5}}

On April 10, 2008, NBC ordered a fifth season consisting of 28 half-hour episodes,<ref>Carter, Bill. [https://www.nytimes.com/2009/01/26/business/media/26network.html?_r=2&ref=business  "New on the Networks: Safe Formulas From the Past".] ''The New York Times''. January 26, 2009.  Retrieved on February 4, 2009.</ref> four of which were paired as two hour-long episodes. The season premiered on September 25, 2008.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://tv.ign.com/objects/142/14244637.html | title=''The Office'': Season 5|website=IGN|access-date=October 1, 2008}}</ref>

This season highlighted Michael's roller coaster relationship with corporate, as he is first praised and rewarded for impressive numbers despite the economic downturn. However, when a new boss is hired Michael feels slighted by his controlling manner.  The theme of the beginning and middle of the season was mostly personal relationships with Dwight, Angela, Andy, Jim, Pam, Michael, Jan, and Holly. However, the theme transformed into career growth, as Ryan, Pam, and Michael set up the Michael Scott Paper Company, Pam and Michael go on a lecture circuit, Charles takes Jan's and Ryan's job, and Jim has trouble getting on with Charles.  The last few episodes of the season focused on relationships once again, with major events taking place in Jim and Pam's relationship, and also with Holly and Michael.
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 5}}

===Season 6 (2009–10)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 6}}

On January 15, 2009, it was announced that NBC renewed the series for a sixth season, consisting of 26 half-hour episodes,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news.aspx?id=8487|title=NBC Extends Scripted Series, Confirms Orders|publisher=the futon critic|access-date=January 20, 2010}}</ref> four of which were paired as two hour-long episodes. The season premiered on September 17, 2009.<ref name=season_6_press>{{cite press release |url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2009/06/25/nbc-announces-fall-series-premiere-dates-31797/20090625nbc01/ |title=NBC Announces Fall Series Premiere Dates |publisher=NBC Universal |access-date=June 26, 2009 |date=June 25, 2009 }}</ref>

Story arcs in the sixth season include Jim becoming co-manager with Michael of the Scranton branch, Michael dating Pam's mother, Dwight attempting to get Jim fired, and Dunder Mifflin facing an uncertain future due to rumors of insolvency, eventually becoming part of a larger corporation called Sabre. The season also prominently features the long-awaited wedding between Jim and Pam, as well as the birth of their first child.
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 6}}

===Season 7 (2010–11)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 7}}
On March 5, 2010, NBC officially announced that it had renewed ''The Office'' for a seventh season, consisting of 26 half-hour episodes, four of which were paired as two hour-long episodes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.officetally.com/the-office-season-7-spoilers|title=The Office Season 7 spoilers and news|work=OfficeTally|access-date=August 27, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbc.com/news/2010/03/05/nbc-gives-pickups-to-thursday-night-comedies-30-rock-the-office-and-community-for-2010-11/ |title=NBC Gives Pickups To Thursday-Night Comedies '30 Rock,' 'The Office' and 'Community' |publisher=NBC |date=March 5, 2010 |access-date=March 6, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100307194133/http://www.nbc.com/news/2010/03/05/nbc-gives-pickups-to-thursday-night-comedies-30-rock-the-office-and-community-for-2010-11/ |archive-date=March 7, 2010 }}</ref> [[Steve Carell]] confirmed the season would be his last on the series.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2010/06/28/steve-carell-office-exit/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101122121500/http://insidetv.ew.com/2010/06/28/steve-carell-office-exit/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 22, 2010|title=Steve Carell on 'Office' exit: 'It's a good time to move on'|author=Michael Ausiello|magazine=Entertainment Weekly|access-date=June 28, 2010|date=June 28, 2010}}</ref> The season premiered on September 23, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbc.com/news/2010/07/15/nbc-announces-series-premiere-dates-for-fall-2010-schedule/ |title=NBC Announces Series Premiere Dates for Fall 2010 Schedule |work=NBC |access-date=July 17, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718090136/http://www.nbc.com/news/2010/07/15/nbc-announces-series-premiere-dates-for-fall-2010-schedule/ |archive-date=July 18, 2010 }}</ref>

The seventh season of ''The Office'' largely revolves around the character development and departure of Michael from the series. After Toby is called for jury duty, Holly returns, causing Michael to once again pursue her, despite her being in a relationship. After eventually proving himself to her, the two get engaged, but Michael decides to move to [[Boulder, Colorado]] to help Holly take care of her elderly parents. After Michael leaves, the office is forced to choose a new manager.
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 7}}

===Season 8 (2011–12)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 8}}
On March 17, 2011, NBC renewed ''The Office'' for an eighth season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hitfix.com/blogs/whats-alan-watching/posts/nbc-renews-the-office-parks-and-recreation-and-community|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110323104657/http://www.hitfix.com/blogs/whats-alan-watching/posts/nbc-renews-the-office-parks-and-recreation-and-community|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 23, 2011|title=NBC renews 'The Office,' 'Parks and Recreation' and 'Community'|work=HitFix|last=Sepinwall|first=Alan|date=March 17, 2011|access-date=March 18, 2011}}</ref> consisting of 24 episodes. This season focuses on [[Andy Bernard]] becoming manager of the Scranton branch, before being replaced as manager by Nellie Bertram ([[Catherine Tate]]) midway through the season. [[James Spader]] also became a regular cast member, playing the role of [[Robert California]], the new CEO of Sabre. Also, Jim and Pam welcome their second child.

The eighth season of ''The Office'' largely centers around the antics of the new Sabre CEO, Robert California. Initially, he appears calm, collected, and calculating. However, as the season progresses, it becomes obvious that his management style is slowly destroying the company. Dwight—along with Jim, Stanley, Ryan, Erin, and [[Cathy Simms|Cathy]] ([[Lindsey Broad]])—travel to Florida to help set up a Sabre Store, where [[Nellie Bertram]] ([[Catherine Tate]]) is introduced. Eventually, former CFO of Dunder Mifflin David Wallace buys back the company, firing California.
{{:The Office (American TV series) season 8}}

===Season 9 (2012–13)===
{{Main|The Office (American TV series) season 9}}
On May 11, 2012, NBC renewed ''The Office'' for a ninth season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/05/11/parks-and-recreation-season-5-nbc_n_1508931.html|title='Parks And Recreation' Renewed: NBC Orders Season 5 And 'The Office' Season 9 And 'Up All Night' Season 2|work=The Huffington Post|date=May 11, 2012|access-date=May 12, 2012}}</ref> which was later announced to be the final season.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2012/08/21/the-office-season-9/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120822062232/http://insidetv.ew.com/2012/08/21/the-office-season-9/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 22, 2012 |title='The Office' will end next season |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |first=James |last=Hibberd |date=August 21, 2012 |access-date=August 21, 2012}}</ref> The season consists of 25 episodes.<ref name=25epsnot24>{{cite web|last=Tan|first=Jennie|title=The Office Season 9 Spoilers and News|url=http://www.officetally.com/the-office-season-9-spoilers-and-news|publisher=OfficeTally|access-date=March 5, 2013|date=March 5, 2013}}</ref>

The ninth season largely focuses on the relationship between Jim and Pam Halpert. After Jim decides to follow his dream and start a sports marketing company in Philadelphia, Pam begins to worry about moving, and the couple's relationship experiences stress. Meanwhile, Andy abandons the office for a three-month boating trip, and eventually quits his job to pursue his dream of becoming a star. Dwight is then promoted to regional manager.

==Webisodes==
===''The Accountants'' (2006)===
NBC announced on March 16, 2006, that there would be ten original, stand-alone [[webisode]] shorts on NBC.com.  They debuted on July 13, and concluded on September 7, 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbc.com/The_Office/video/categories/the-accountants/33180/ |publisher=NBC.com |access-date=August 25, 2008 |title=Webisodes : ''The Accountants'' |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080825102129/http://www.nbc.com/The_Office/video/categories/the-accountants/33180/ |archive-date=August 25, 2008 }}</ref> They were directed by [[Randall Einhorn]] and written by [[Michael Schur]] and [[Paul Lieberstein]], and were edited by Michael Zurer, an assistant editor on the series. It took two days to film them,<ref>{{cite web| url=http://tv.ign.com/articles/718/718200p2.html |title=Exclusive Interview: ''The Office'' Webisode Writers|website= [[IGN]]|access-date=April 22, 2008|author=Zoromski, Brian|date=July 12, 2006}}</ref> and in June 2007, ''The Accountants'' won the Comedy Short Award at the inaugural [[Webby Awards]] and  a [[Daytime Emmy Award]] for Outstanding Broadband Program – Comedy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.emmyonline.org/mediacenter/daytime_34th_creative_winners_data.html |title=34th Annual Creative Arts & Entertainment Emmy Awards |publisher=EmmyOnline |date=June 14, 2007 |access-date=April 22, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071209182633/http://www.emmyonline.org/mediacenter/daytime_34th_creative_winners_data.html |archive-date=December 9, 2007 }}</ref>  In November 2007, the webisodes became a point of argument for the [[Writers Guild of America, East|Writers Guild of America]] for [[2007 Writers Guild of America Strike|the 2007 strike]], as none of the writers or actors featured in the webisodes were paid residuals for their participation.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://weblogs.variety.com/wga_strike_blog/2007/11/greg-daniels-we.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110520202254/http://weblogs.variety.com/wga_strike_blog/2007/11/greg-daniels-we.html |archive-date=May 20, 2011 |work=Variety |access-date=August 23, 2008 |title=Greg Daniels: We've seen the future, and it is us |date=November 7, 2007}}</ref>

Major characters Michael, Jim and Pam do not appear in ''The Accountants'' webisodes. Instead, the focus is on the three members of the accounting department: Oscar, Angela and Kevin—who appear in each webisode—as they try to find $3000 missing from the office budget. The series won an [[Emmy Award]] in the "Outstanding Broadband Program – Comedy" category at the [[34th Daytime Emmy Awards]] in 2007. Tim Stack of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' graded the series with an "A−" and wrote, "While we miss [[Jim Halpert|Jim]] and [[Pam Beesly|Pam]] (not to mention star [[Steve Carell]]), these shorts prove that spending time with their excessively awkward co-workers can be just as sweet."<ref>{{cite magazine| url=http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1228401,00.html| magazine=Entertainment Weekly| access-date=2008-08-24| title=''The Office'': Webisodes (TV Review)| author=Stack, Tim| date=2006-08-18| archive-date=October 3, 2008| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081003042956/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1228401,00.html| url-status=dead}}</ref>

===''Kevin's Loan'' (2008)===
NBC ordered a new set of [[webisodes]] for the summer of 2008.  The webisode series began its run on July 10, 2008, and ended on July 31, 2008. The webisodes feature Kevin, who pursues a unique solution in an effort to pay back his looming gambling debts. The other characters who appeared are Oscar, Stanley and Darryl.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2008/05/12/nbc-digital-entertainment-serves-up-users-favorites-27531/20080512nbc03/ |title=NBC Digital Entertainment Serves Up Users' Favorites|publisher=NBC Universal |access-date=August 24, 2008 | date= May 12, 2008}}</ref>

===''The Outburst'' (2008)===
NBC ordered a new set of [[webisodes]] for the winter of 2008.  The webisode series began its run on November 20, 2008. The webisodes feature all of ''The Office'' characters except for [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael]], [[Pam Beesly|Pam]], [[Jim Halpert|Jim]], [[Dwight Schrute|Dwight]] and [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan]]. [[Oscar Martinez (The Office)|Oscar]] has an outburst in the middle of the office and his coworkers start an investigation.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.officetally.com/the-office-webisodes-the-outburst?page=1&cp=1#comments |title=The Office Webisodes: The Outburst|publisher=NBC Universal |access-date=November 24, 2008 | date= November 24, 2008}}</ref>

===''The 3rd Floor'' (2010)===
Ryan attempts to make a horror film titled ''The 3rd Floor'' using Dunder Mifflin as a location, and workers such as Kelly, Erin, Gabe, Kevin and Meredith as actors. ''The 3rd Floor'' was written by Jonathan Hughes, Kelly Hannon and Mary Wall and directed by Mindy Kaling.

===''The Podcast'' (2011)===
Gabe attempts to record a podcast in the office about the Sabre website, hoping to impress corporate. The webisodes were made available on January 20, 2011, on NBC.com, but were previously included on the season 6 DVD release.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.officetally.com/the-office-webisodes-the-podcast|title=The Office Webisodes: The Podcast|work=OfficeTally|date=January 20, 2011|access-date=January 21, 2011}}</ref>

===''The Girl Next Door'' (2011)===
The series focuses on Kelly and Erin's girl group called Subtle Sexuality. The first webisode documents the behind-the-scenes aspects of their second single "The Girl Next Door", while the second and final webisode is the music video itself, which features Ryan. The webisodes were made available on May 4, 2011, on NBC.com.
